newsitem.title: UK: B.A.T gains on talk of U.S. tobacco deal.
newsitem.headline: B.A.T gains on talk of U.S. tobacco deal.

text.p: Shares in B.A.T Industries climbed on Thursday amid growing speculation that the U.S. tobacco industry looked set to conclude a landmark deal to resolve tobacco-related lawsuits today.
The shares were 8p higher at 576p by 0828 GMT after opening slightly lower on the day.
"There are strong rumours of a tobacco settlement which is helping the stock," said one senior trader
Analysts estimate that the industry could face claims totalling $300 billion from smokers and state governments claiming healthcare costs.
B.A.T owns Brown & Williamson Tobacco Corp, the third largest cigarette maker in the U.S.
John Nuttall, tobacco analyst at Panmure Gordon said the key element he would be looking for in any settlement would be whether the industry receives immunity from future litigation.
"If it does receive this kind of immunity it will be a big coup for the industry," he said. "But any sort of compromise would clearly be disappointing."
"If the rumours are true and depending on the nature of the agreement I would expect the shares to rise significantly," said Nuttall. "Certainly above the six pounds level."
